doc.title: Nicki Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe. Utica, New York, November 6, 2010 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Love of the road and funny times with Les Paul
summary: Musicians are good company and the road gives the best times; she recalls watching Les Paul handle celebrities and a payment problem backstage.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Well you have to be passionate about music to make a living at it, isn’t that right?

Oh absolutely. You’ve got to love it and I love the music community. And the best musicians are, oh most musicians are really mostly good people to be around and hang out with. You know? The best times in my life are times on the road. And the funniest times in my life are times on the road.
Like can you pull one out of your memory? I know that’s a hard question.
No it is, it’s really hard to do that.

Because what happens with that, it’s like saying an Australian expression. I have to be in the mood or someone has to remind me of something to spur that on and it’s hard to do that. There were really funny times watching Les Paul be the road. Now here he’s like 90 years old and he’s going out to California and just to watch him around the celebrities and people that came to the gig and just to see how he handled it, and then if there was a problem with the money and watching him just stand backstage and not go on stage, whatever. And people waiting for us. And there were times where I was like, this is interesting. And then the bus came back and they sorted it all out and then all right, then we’ll go back on. We didn’t know exactly what happened but it was all okay. Stuff like that. There were so many times when like, wow.
